items.question_text:
The position-time (x–t) graph of an object moving in one dimension consists of straight-line segments passing through the points (0 s, 0 m), (2.5 s, 50 m), (7.5 s, 50 m), (10.0 s, 100 m), and (15.0 s, 0 m). Using this information, calculate:
(a) the average velocity over the time interval from 0 to 10 s
(b) the instantaneous velocity at the time instants t = 2 s, t = 5 s, t = 8 s, and t = 12 s
items.figure_description: A graph of position x (in m) plotted against time t (in s). The curve starts at (0, 0), rises with a constant positive slope to (2.5, 50), stays horizontal at x = 50 until t = 7.5, continues upward linearly to (10.0, 100), and then descends linearly to meet the time axis at (15.0, 0).

items.question_text: An elevator begins moving upward from a stationary state, with its acceleration changing over time as shown in the given graph. The acceleration is 2 ms⁻² between t = 0 and t = 4 s, remains 0 from t = 4 s to t = 8 s, and is −2 ms⁻² between t = 8 s and t = 12 s. Determine the total vertical displacement of the elevator from its initial level by the time it stops.
items.figure_description: An acceleration-time graph showing acceleration a in ms⁻² on the vertical axis and time t in s on the horizontal axis. A horizontal line segment extends from t = 0 to t = 4 s at a = 2 ms⁻². The curve lies on the time axis (a = 0) from t = 4 s to t = 8 s. A horizontal line segment extends from t = 8 s to t = 12 s at a = −2 ms⁻².

items.question_text: An object possesses an initial velocity v₀ = 10 ms⁻¹ and is subjected to a deceleration of magnitude 0.2v², where v represents its instantaneous velocity. What will be the velocity of the object at t = 2 s?

A particle travels along a straight horizontal line with its velocity expressed as v = (3t² − 6t) m/s, where t is the time in seconds. Starting from the origin at t = 0, calculate the following for the duration between t = 0 and t = 3.5 s:
(a) The total distance covered by the particle
(b) The average velocity of the particle
(c) The average speed of the particle

An object travels along a circular path having a radius of 4 cm at a uniform speed of 1 cm/s. Determine:
(a) The time period of revolution for the object.
(b) The magnitudes of the average speed, average velocity, and average acceleration over the duration from t = 0 to t = T/4, where T denotes the time period.

A particle travels along a straight path such that its speed v decreases as a linear function of position s, starting at 20 m/s when s = 0 and reaching zero at s = 30 m. Find the acceleration of the body at the position s = 15 m.

A particle, initially at rest, begins rectilinear motion with a uniform acceleration. When a duration t₀ has elapsed, the direction of this acceleration is reversed while its magnitude remains unchanged. Find the total elapsed time T from the start until the particle arrives back at its starting point.

At the same instant, two bodies, A and B, travel along a straight path in an identical direction. Particle A has an initial speed of 3 m/s and maintains a constant acceleration of 1 m/s², while particle B has an initial speed of 1 m/s and an acceleration of 2 m/s². If particle A begins at a position 10 m behind particle B, determine the closest distance of approach between the two particles.

From a height of 12 m, a ball is projected straight up with an initial speed of 18 m/s. Exactly at this moment, an open-platform lift crosses the 5 m mark while ascending at a steady speed of 2 m/s. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², calculate:
(a) the time and location where the ball encounters the platform,
(b) the velocity of the ball measured relative to the platform upon collision.

Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion and Reason. Choose the appropriate option that describes them.

Assertion: Based on the formula a = v(dv/ds), whenever the velocity of a body equals zero, its acceleration must likewise vanish.
Reason: The quantity a defined in this expression represents the instantaneous acceleration.

options.label: a
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

options.label: b
options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

options.label: c
options.text: Assertion is true, but Reason is false.

options.label: d
options.text: Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

items.question_text:
A particle travels within the x-y plane such that its position coordinates at instant t are given by (2t, t²). Determine:
(a) the equation of the particle's trajectory,
(b) its velocity at time t, and
(c) its acceleration at any instant t.

The position of an object travelling across the xy-plane is given as a function of time by x = 2t² and y = t³, where coordinates x and y are measured in metres and time t is in seconds. Determine the average acceleration of the object over the duration from t = 0 to t = 2 s.

A particle moving in the x-y plane experiences a time-dependent acceleration described by a = (2t î + 3t² ĵ) m/s². At the moment t = 0, it begins moving from the origin with an initial velocity of 2 m/s directed along the positive x-axis. Determine the velocity vector and the position coordinates of the particle at t = 1 s.

A body is thrown vertically upward with an initial speed of 40 m/s. Taking the upward direction as positive and assuming g = 10 m/s², draw the acceleration-time (a-t), velocity-time (v-t), and displacement-time (s-t) curves representing its entire motion until it returns to the launch level.
(a) Acceleration-time (a-t) graph
(b) Velocity-time (v-t) graph
(c) Displacement-time (s-t) graph
items.figure_description:
Three kinematic graphs from t = 0 s to t = 8 s:
1. a-t graph: A horizontal line at a = −10 m/s² spanning from t = 0 s to t = 8 s.
2. v-t graph: A straight line with a constant negative slope beginning at (0 s, +40 m/s), intersecting the time axis at (4 s, 0 m/s), and ending at (8 s, −40 m/s).
3. s-t graph: An inverted parabola starting at the origin (0 s, 0 m), reaching a peak at (4 s, 80 m), and returning to zero at (8 s, 0 m).

items.question_text: The position of an object traveling along a straight path varies with time according to the relation x = 32t − (8/3)t³, where the coordinate x is in metres and time t is in seconds. Determine its acceleration at the moment it momentarily comes to a stop.

An object is thrown straight up into the air with a starting speed of 40 m/s. Determine both its total displacement and the overall distance it travels during the first 6 s of its flight. (Use g = 10 m/s²)
